analysis: The PR is documentation-only. docs/architecture/security/encryption.md (head text only, no diff supplied) now has a "Provider cache storage" section (head lines 176-235) covering DBK3 encrypted SSD cache payloads, the `darkbloom cache set --directory` volume checks, and an operator storage recommendation. docs/consumer/verification.md (head 253-255) and docs/provider/attestation.md (patch @@ -321) each gain the same three-line note: local cache-volume checks are storage suitability checks, not peripheral firmware authenticity, and not part of the coordinator's attestation verdict. The anchor `#provider-cache-storage` exists in encryption.md. The notes do not alter coordinator authorization, App Attest, legacy MDM, dispatch or encryption behaviour (TB-002, TB-009, TB-011, T-052..T-058 are unchanged). The notes also avoid overclaiming: they state that TTL is not anti-rollback, that the filesystem UUID pin can be cloned, and that the checks are not peripheral attestation. The prelude field-minimization and encryption-hop text matches the canonical header, so I found no contradiction. One item for later passes: T-041 (SSD cache, oversized, not fully visible) should be checked for coverage of the external-volume threats now documented: cloned filesystem UUID, a malicious controller retaining ciphertext, and rollback or replay of still-valid ciphertext. That is a possible threat-model sync gap, not a PR regression. No code or config was supplied, so claims about the cache-volume implementation (CacheVolume, CacheStorage in the cited Swift files) are unverified. Nothing in these changes weakens an existing control.
